thread:
alex k: Quick heads-up — proposing credential-affinity throttling for Redwood serving. idea is to route requests with the same service-account/org/project to the same shard/pool to keep KV/prefix cache warm and apply per-credential throttles. want opinions before I draft a canary plan.

jamie r: can you TL;DR the benefits vs risks? :eyes:

alex k: benefits: higher cache-hit-rate => lower p50/p95 latency and token-cost. easier to reason about per-key QoS. risks: hot keys could monopolize a shard, making tail latency worse for others, and quota enforcement becomes more complex.

maria t: sounds useful for workloads with strong locality (chat sessions pinned to sa). how do we avoid monopolies?

alex k: two levers: 1) per-credential soft throttle (qps + burst), 2) global fair-share guardrail across the pool. default fair-share backoff if key exceeds share.

sasha p: how does this interact with existing quota/console? we already have per-org/per-project quotas and console dashboards.

alex k: proposal: map affinity to the lowest non-null identity in precedence (service-account -> project -> org). apply per-credential throttle based on configured bucket. quota still aggregates exactly the same for billing; affinity only affects routing and local throttling. console shows both aggregated quota and shard-affinity telemetry.

leo w: telemetry we should emit immediately: affinity_cache_hit_ratio, affinity_shard_load, per_cred_throttle_events, per_cred_tail_latency. want these before any rollout.

maria t: +1 for metrics. also add "affinity_evictions" to track when we break affinity due to capacity.

alex k: good call. sample config we were thinking about: 
```
affinity:
  enabled: true
  key_precedence: ["service_account", "project", "org"]
  per_credential_throttle:
    qps: 20
    burst: 80
  shard_guard:
    max_share_percent: 30
```

jamie r: UX question: should teams be able to opt-out at org or project level from affinity? some customers run multi-tenant noisy workloads.

alex k: yes — make it opt-in per org by default off for now. add console toggle and an org-level flag so SEs can flip it for specific customers. rollout plan: canary 1% orgs -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%. watch metrics Leo listed plus error-rate and CPU/GPU utilization.

sasha p: about throttles: if a credential hits limit, do we want to 429 or queue? queueing on the serving side is messy. I'd prefer immediate 429 with helpful error code and retry-after header.

maria t: also expose the throttle budget in SDK responses so clients can backoff smarter.

leo w: implement internal telemetry tag: "affinity_mode=credential" so we can diff against baseline. we should also emit per-key sample traces for p99 investigation.

infra-bot: deploy-plan created: infra/affinity-throttle/canary-1pct (id: dp-20260321-71)

jamie r: edge case: ephemeral API keys (short-lived) — affinity would create cold shards if keys rotate rapidly. how do we detect ephemeral keys and skip affinity?

alex k: detect by TTL metadata when present; also heuristic: high churn key rate -> bypass affinity and treat as stateless. we'll add a metric "credential_churn_rate".

sasha p: telemetry alert thresholds we want before canary: affinity_cache_hit_ratio drops >5% vs baseline, per_shard_cpu>85%, any org experiencing >10% increased p95 latency, and sustained per_cred_throttle_events for top-10 keys.

maria t: who owns the console changes? I'll volunteer to prototype the toggle and new panels for affinity_shard_load and per-cred throttles.

alex k: thanks — Maria to own console mock, Leo to own metrics instrumentation, Sasha to own throttle semantics (429 + headers), Jamie to own rollout docs and canary checklist. I'll implement routing logic and shard_guard.

leo w: note — for billing we must keep aggregation identical so customers see same token usage regardless of affinity routing. don't change accounting.

alex k: confirmed. billing team will be unchanged.

jamie r: one more: expose an admin API to migrate an org off affinity if we detect problems mid-rollout. need an emergency kill switch.

alex k: yes — emergency kill switch + per-org override. add to runbook.

infra-bot: canary job started for dp-20260321-71 — 1% of orgs targeted.

sasha p: OK let's run with this. will draft throttle error semantics doc and add example SDK snippet for retrying on 429.

maria t: I'll post console mock this afternoon. if no blockers by EOD tomorrow we start 1% canary. :thumbsup:

alex k: sweet. thanks team.

jamie r: +1
notes: decision: proceed with credential-affinity routing + per-credential soft throttles, console opt-in, 1%->5%->25%->100% canary, telemetry and emergency kill-switch required. owners assigned: alex (routing), maria (console), leo (metrics), sasha (throttle semantics), jamie (rollout docs).
